title: Two helper skills can't lose their only trigger: how should FR-3 be met?
context: FR-3 and AC-3 say retest-verification stops triggering on pentest-retest and site-map-retest stops triggering on site-map-retest. That workflow is the only trigger each has. The skill parser (src/skills/frontmatter-parser.ts) rejects a skill with no triggers unless it has request_routing, and tests/unit/content/skills-structure.test.ts requires the same, so removing it makes the skill fail to parse. The spec's non-goals also say routing and helper procedures stay unchanged.

options.label: Allow an explicit 'triggers: []' for a helper only its parent calls. Small change to the parser and the structure test, which the frozen spec does not list; a missing triggers key still fails. AC-3 is met as written.
options.one_line_preview: Allow an explicit 'triggers: []' for a helper only its parent calls. Small change to the parser and the structure test, which the frozen spec does not list; a missing triggers key still fails. AC-3 is met as written.
options.trade_off: Not stated when the decision was opened.

options.label: Keep the trigger on both helpers and change FR-3 and AC-3. No code change, but a retest request loads the parent and the helper together, the risk the skill-orchestrator expert raised.
options.one_line_preview: Keep the trigger on both helpers and change FR-3 and AC-3. No code change, but a retest request loads the parent and the helper together, the risk the skill-orchestrator expert raised.
options.trade_off: Not stated when the decision was opened.

options.label: Give each helper a trigger on another dimension that never matches. It passes the parser with no code change, but the metadata then says something untrue.

rationale: Owner chose: allow an explicit empty trigger list for a helper only its parent calls. A missing triggers key still fails.
